reasons: The excerpt explicitly presents a money-back guarantee as a table-stakes risk reversal positioned after proof, for customers who still do not trust the brand.
The candidate preserves the source's limited scope and does not invent guarantee terms, duration, or return conditions.
The excerpt says the illustrated page could be improved with more direct before-and-after testimonials and gives four across slightly different demographics as an aspirational example.
The candidate correctly qualifies the approximate count as illustrative rather than mandatory.
The recommendation to consult the site transcribed as bayard.com for cart-abandonment research is supported by the excerpt.

However, the action additionally instructs the operator to verify the site name/URL. The excerpt does not recommend verification; it only states the name as "bayard.com." Keep URL uncertainty as an unknown or source limitation rather than adding it as a required action.
The source explicitly says all additional expenses added at checkout—not only shipping—should be below 10% of average order value.
The candidate includes the source's qualification that this is an internal rule of thumb that may vary by brand and can be tested lower.
The excerpt offers faster actual delivery and fast delivery options at checkout as alternatives when slow delivery contributes to abandonment.
The candidate retains the source's feasibility caveat concerning regional areas with poor shipping times and does not invent a delivery-speed threshold.
The excerpt characterizes card-detail distrust as a trust issue and expressly calls for more social proof and brand presence.
It also specifically frames avoiding a scam-like website and reinforcing good proof as advice for startups and new brands, which the candidate retains.
The excerpt states that photo reviews were sorted first in the depicted stronger, right-hand landing-page example.

It does not expressly generalize this depiction into a universal recommendation to sort photo reviews first on all landing pages. Reframe the unit as an attribute of the illustrated stronger layout, or supply source text that makes the broader instruction explicit.

omissions.description: Where a suitably supported specific callout can be used, the source presents it as beneficial, while explicitly questioning whether the skin-firmness percentage in the example can actually be validated.
omissions.quote: Now, I don't know how we actually validate firmness of skin through a percentage, but if we can do something like this, anytime we can have a specific call out, it's always great.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-thought, so preceding context for the opening statement is absent.
The excerpt ends mid-sentence after discussing transparent total cost, so its final recommendation and any qualifications are incomplete.

The abandonment percentages, the claimed browsing share, the 10% threshold, and the cited research site's findings are asserted in the excerpt without study methodology, definitions, or supporting evidence.
The site name appears only as the transcription "bayard.com"; the excerpt itself provides no confirmation of its spelling or current URL.
The source explicitly states uncertainty about validating a skin-firmness percentage, so that example does not establish a substantiated measurement method.
